intro: A useful tree split separates class mixtures. Compare every gap in a numeric feature using the weighted impurity of its two children.
task: Find the best binary split of one feature using Gini impurity, with deterministic threshold and class ties.
requirements: values and labels are equal-length vectors with at least two observations. Labels are zero or one and values must contain at least two distinct numbers.
Candidate thresholds are midpoints of consecutive distinct sorted values. Left rows satisfy value<=threshold. Minimize child-size-weighted Gini impurity 1-sum(class_probability**2).

Return {"threshold": threshold, "impurity": weighted_impurity, "gain": parent_impurity-weighted_impurity, "left_class": majority_left, "right_class": majority_right}. Impurity ties within 1e-12 choose the smaller threshold; class ties choose zero.
If a floating-point midpoint rounds up to the upper endpoint, use the largest representable value below that endpoint so both children remain nonempty.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Distinct sorted values define all possible changes to the partition; gaps are enough to enumerate candidates.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Weight each child impurity by its sample count before comparing candidates, then resolve ties consistently.

explanation: Each candidate is judged by the impurity remaining after the split, weighted by child sample counts. An unweighted average could overvalue a tiny pure child.
Thresholds inside a gap create the same partition, so midpoints give a reproducible representative. Ties are resolved explicitly to keep training deterministic.
